newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds firm on back of U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds firm on back of U.S. data.

text.p: Irish bonds firmed in late trade on Tuesday on the back of market-friendly U.S. data after a bad start to the day, dealers said.

"It's been a topsy-turvy session," one dealer said. "Irish bonds were underperforming severely at the short-end this morning due to an increase in money market rates but cheered up considerably following excellent data out of the U.S."
Trade volumes later in the session had been very steady, dealers said, adding that while Irish bonds were firmer on the day, in a relative sense they were underperforming most other markets.
Shorter-dated bonds were affected by a further rise in interbank rates this morning following protracted punt-selling by the market, dealers said.
Over the past week the Central bank has tightened interbank rates in response to the weakness of the currency.
While today's U.S. data showed consumer demand was still strong, the bulk of it showed inflationary pressures to be easing, which in turn calmed interest rate worries.

The data included the first quarter Employment Cost Index which rose 0.6 percent compared with forecasts of around 0.9 percent. March durable goods orders fell by an unexpected 3.0 percent, compared with forecasts of orders being unchanged.
However, dealers pointed out the importance of Friday's payrolls numbers which, if strong would make a near term rates hike almost certain.

By 1500 GMT, the 6.5 percent bond due 2001 was up 14 pence from Monday's close at 101.70 to yield 5.96 percent while the key benchmark eight percent bond due 2006 had gained 36 pence from the close to 108.36 to yield 6.64 percent.

Dealer said Irish bonds were yielding 151 basis points over German bunds in the five-year area - a widening of three basis points from Monday's close - and 92 basis points over Germany in the 10-year area, a widening of two basis points.
